The unknown reading is the one the old precondition wrongly excluded, and on a cluster whose agentgateway controller is renamed it is every pass, permanently. `policyBrokenMessage` branches the lead on which clause fired: the synthetic ancestor and an explicit `Attached=False` keep that lead and "the hole is announced, not closed"; `Accepted=False` says the Gateway rejected the policy outright, so none of this Agent's authentication or authorization is in force; `Accepted=True` with a reason other than `Valid` says the Gateway accepted the policy **but not the whole of it**, says in terms that the Gateway is NOT reporting it unattached AT THE POLICY'S CURRENT GENERATION — not “on this pass”, which overstates a reading the generation gate makes narrower, and which matters because `Attached` was measured lagging `Accepted` by a generation on 1.5.0 — and that this judgement issues no request so whether a credential is still required is not established either way, and sends the reader to the Gateway's own reason **and message**, with the key-`ConfigMap` attribution and its namespace-wide blast radius HEDGED — 1.5.0 reports the same `PartiallyValid` for three measured causes and only that one is shared; and a HELD report, which re-derived no clause, says that it is restating a claim it cannot narrow. **Whether it ALSO says what the Gateway has done since belongs to the NOTE, not the lead, and there are THREE held paths rather than two**: the Gateway gone quiet at this object's generation, and an errored `-auth` step, both say it and both checked it — `heldNote` and `erroredNote`. The third, where §5's precondition excluded the policy, must not, and gets `unjudgedNote`; leaving `heldNote` on it put “the Gateway has not reported since” into the same message as “nothing here will clear this claim”, one message and two claims with the second never checked (A83). **§5's precondition is stated only where the pass established it** (`policyJudgedNote`): a claim held over a pass that read no policy — every pass after a foreign takeover of the `-auth` name, and every pass after an upgrade whose render digest is not the one `status.auth` records — gets a `why` naming both exclusions and saying that nothing here will clear it. **Two clauses can fire on one policy, and then the STRONGER claim's words win** — non-attachment over rejection over partial acceptance — which moves no answer, because the report is broken on any of them. **The REASON does not branch**: `AuthPolicyNotAttached` on both conditions for every clause, which is (B1) kept and D5(b) decided as no, because the claim store is one boolean per half and carries no clause, so a per-clause reason could not be re-asserted on a pass that re-derives nothing (§5, §9 D5, A83). **It is a control-plane fix and reads no request**, so it cannot tell a `PartiallyValid` that left authentication working from one that disabled it. **When the route half fires on the same pass — which it does in A80's own measured incident, because renaming the listener detaches the route AND leaves `<agent>-auth` attached to nothing — `PolicyApplyIncomplete`, `Ready` and `Degraded` read `ServingRouteNotAccepted` instead, **and only `PolicyApplyIncomplete`'s message also names `AuthPolicyNotAttached`** — `withholdInOrder` keeps the outranking failure's message whole, so `Ready` and `Degraded` carry the route half's message alone (this sentence said all three named it until A84's second revision measured otherwise) — and the policy half's own text stops asserting that the route is accepted and serving**: nothing reaches the agent on that pass, so the claim the fail-open half makes cannot be true. `GovernanceSkipped` still reads `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, because it is the condition that records the tier (A81; §5, case 19 (q)). Nothing is withdrawn, deleted or rewritten, for the reason the missing-policy `Lock` gives: withdrawing would hand anyone who can edit the Gateway a switch that takes the Agent off the air. **The hole is announced, not closed**, and the message says so. **This state was inferred until A82 measured it (§8.1), and what it measured is below.** §3.3.2 records the upstream fixture in which a policy whose target route **does not yet exist** reports `Accepted=True` beside `Attached=False` with `output: []`; a served Agent cannot be in that state, because `reconcileServed` re-asserts its route every pass. The served case — an existing, accepted route beside a policy the Gateway reports broken — was inferred from the same reporting shape, of which `StatusSummary` is §3.3.2's general form, **and A82 has now measured it on agentgateway 1.5.0** (§8.1, `research/a80-policy-half-conformance-2026-09.md`). Both reachable shapes are real on an accepted route, and they answer differently: a byte-unchanged policy reported `Accepted=True`/`PartiallyValid` leaves the route refusing anonymous requests `401`, and a policy reported `Attached=False` on `StatusSummary` leaves it answering `200`. **The bypass shape was reached by editing the policy's own `targetRefs`, and A82's first draft read that as putting it outside the precondition above. THAT IS BACKWARDS, and the bullet two sentences up says why: the comparison is RENDER AGAINST RENDER — `reassertServedPolicy` digests what `compiler.AuthPolicy` renders for this Agent, never the stored object, and compares it to `appliedDigest`, which is itself a render digest — so it is INVARIANT under any out-of-band edit to the live policy.** The state is therefore judged, and **the state is entered, REPAIRED on the first pass after the edit, and REPORTED on whichever pass first reads the synthetic ancestor — which may be before that pass, with it, or after it**. The three orderings are one mechanism and not three: the guards pass whatever the status says, `writeAuthPolicy` overwrites the drifted `spec`, and `judgeServed` raises on a synthetic ancestor it does not generation-gate, so a report can arrive for a generation already superseded. On a cluster the edit's own event usually lands first, so the earliest pass repairs while raising nothing and a later one reports about a state already repaired. §8.1 case 19 (f) writes the ancestor BEFORE reconciling and so pins the CO-LOCATION — that one pass both raises and repairs — which is the property the conclusion needs and not the ordering. **The window is one watch round-trip**: the policy watch is label-selected with no predicate (`internal/controller/gatewaywiring.go`), so the out-of-band edit itself enqueues the Agent, and nothing waits on a resync. The measured `200` is a window between the edit and the pass that repairs it, not a standing hole. **A80's premise is satisfied, not falsified**: the case is the fixture A80 said did not exist. §8.1 case 19 (f) pins the sequence. Nothing tried produced `Accepted=False` on a policy, and nothing tried produced `Attached=False` on the REAL Gateway ancestor either — the shape case 19 (f)'s `unattachPolicy` writes — so both are the CRD's word and neither is a measurement. **And the synthetic ancestor means LESS than this judgement assumes**: on a policy with two `targetRefs` of which one does not resolve, 1.5.0 writes BOTH ancestors at the current generation — the synthetic one for the ref that failed and the real Gateway's, `Attached=True`, for the one that resolved — and the route enforces, `401`. The short-circuit above would report `AuthPolicyNotAttached` against a contemporaneous `Attached=True`, and its justification — "the last thing the Gateway said is that this policy attached to nothing" — is false there. It is unreachable for an `<agent>-auth`, which the compiler gives exactly one `targetRef`, **and that is the mechanism behind the negative result above**: for one ref, a synthetic ancestor and non-attachment do coincide, and the only ways to make that ref fail are to remove the route — and then the route half does NOT fire, because `recreateRoute` puts a `Create` in the slot and the served judgement runs only on an empty slot or a refused `Adopt`; the way out is the `Create` path — or to edit the ref, which the first pass after the edit repairs, and **the bound on that sentence, which a reader would otherwise act on wrongly**: an identity that can write the policy can strip `assayd.dev/agent-uid` and repoint `targetRefs` in ONE patch, after which §3.2's name-and-label rule makes the object not this Agent's, nothing raises, and the route serves unauthenticated **standing, not a window**. That is the name-and-label rule working as designed and is not introduced by A82, but the repair claim above is true only of an edit that leaves the UID in place. Certainty about the remaining shapes needs agentgateway's source, not more stimuli. The short-circuit is **STILL OWED** a decision — D5(c), and the human's (B1)+(B4) of 2026-09-23 did not take it: A83 splits the message and leaves the short-circuit exactly as it is, so a policy carrying the synthetic ancestor beside a real one reporting `Attached=True` still takes the non-attachment lead (§8.1 owed item 3, §9 D5).

**What the policy half writes, on each route reading and each clause (A84).** Derived from `judgeServed`, `policyBrokenMessage`, `holdIncomplete`, `raiseIncomplete`, `withholdInOrder` and `appendGovernance` (`internal/controller/authserved.go`, `internal/controller/authtxn.go`), and measured on envtest on 2026-09-23 by a throwaway row, not committed, that drove each of the twelve combinations of the first table's four rows and the second table's first three once; the second table's HELD row is read from the code and was not driven. **The tables are measured, not pinned**: committed rows pin the REFUSED × `clauseUnattached` cell (case 19 (q), `TestBothHalvesOnOnePassNameTheRouteFirst`), the hedge on an UNKNOWN reading with a policy claim standing (its `"an unknown route reading hedges too"` subtest), the route half's hold (`TestAnUnknownReadingHoldsAStandingReport`), and each lead of `policyBrokenMessage` in isolation (`TestThePolicyMessageNamesWhatTheGatewaySaid`); the UNKNOWN-with-no-claim × `clauseUnattached` cell as a FIRST raise (§8.1 item 7, `"a first report on an unknown route reading raises"`), and, since A84's third revision, the REFUSED × `clausePartlyValid` cell — the one round 1's BLOCKER turned on — by `TestAServedPolicyTheGatewayDoesNotAttachIsReported`'s `"… on a refused route"` subtest (§8.1 item 10). Since A85, the UNKNOWN-with-no-claim cell of both hedged clauses, `clauseUnattached` and `clauseRejected`, is pinned by `TestTheHedgeSaysWhatWasReadOfTheRoute` (§8.1 item 11), and the HELD policy half beside a same-pass `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` by `TestAHeldPolicyClaimKeepsTheReasonAboveIt` (§8.1 item 9). Nothing committed pins the route half's note being dropped on `GovernanceSkipped`, the `ObservedGeneration` restamp below, or the other cells as combinations. For those no falsifier has been measured, so they are recorded rather than owed — §8.1 owes rows only with one. **This sentence said the same of every cell until the round-2 independent critique measured a falsifier for the partly-valid one** (`reviews/03-a84-critique-r2.md` MAJOR 2). Both tables assume nothing else stands on the pass: no `AuthPolicyMissing`, `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` reason, no deadline, NACK or write-error reason, and no `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` on `GovernanceSkipped`, each of which composes by `incompleteOrder` or `appendGovernance` as stated elsewhere in this section — **and, since A85, where the policy half is HELD (the third table) too.** Until A85 it did not, and that was a defect in shipped code, not in these tables: `holdGovernance` re-asserted a stored `GovernanceSkipped=AuthPolicyNotAttached` whole through `conds.carry`, which OVERWROTE a `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` that `reportForeign` or `reportAboveServed` asserted earlier on the same pass. Measured on envtest on 2026-09-23: a raised policy claim, then `assayd.dev/agent-uid` stripped from `<agent>-auth` and two passes — `PolicyApplyIncomplete` and `Ready` read `ForeignTrafficPolicy`, and `GovernanceSkipped` read `AuthPolicyNotAttached` with the held lead and never named the foreign policy, contrary to §5's rule that a standing `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` keeps the reason. It was rule 8 on the tier condition — it stayed `True`, so it was not fail-open, but it named the wrong cause, on exactly the takeover path the held `why` sends its reader to `GovernanceSkipped` for. A85 carries the stored condition whole only when this pass has not already asserted one of those two reasons, and appends the held claim through `appendGovernance` otherwise (§8.1 item 9, the `GovernanceSkipped` bullet below). **The policy half is raised in every row**: `status.auth.policyUnattached` is set, `PolicyApplyIncomplete=True` and `GovernanceSkipped=True` carry `AuthPolicyNotAttached` somewhere, `Ready` is withheld and the phase is `Degraded`. A route reading is ACCEPTED when `routeReport` answers `reportHolding`, REFUSED when it answers `reportBroken`, and UNKNOWN when it answers `reportUnknown`: no route object; no `status.parents` entry for the assayd Gateway written by agentgateway's `controllerName` (none at all, or only another controller's); or an entry in which `Accepted` and `ResolvedRefs` are not both reported at the route's current generation — one missing, or behind — while neither reads `False` there.

| Route reading | Route half | `PolicyApplyIncomplete` | `Ready`, `Degraded` | `GovernanceSkipped` | Claim store after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACCEPTED | clears `routeRefused`, raises nothing | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`; the message is the policy half's | `False` and `True`, both reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, both with the policy half's message | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`; the message is the policy half's | `routeRefused=false`, `policyUnattached=true` |
| REFUSED | raises `ServingRouteNotAccepted` | reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`; the policy half's message follows ` \| AuthPolicyNotAttached: ` | both reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, both with the route half's message ALONE — `withholdInOrder` keeps the outranking failure's message, so neither names the policy half | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`; the route half's note is overwritten by the policy half's write and does not appear | both `true` |
| UNKNOWN, no `routeRefused` standing | nothing | as ACCEPTED | as ACCEPTED | as ACCEPTED | `routeRefused=false`, `policyUnattached=true` |
| UNKNOWN, `routeRefused` standing | holds `ServingRouteNotAccepted` from stored status, with `heldNote` | reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`; the held route message, then the policy half's, as REFUSED. `LastTransitionTime` is kept; `ObservedGeneration` is NOT (below) | both reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, both with the HELD route message alone | as REFUSED | both `true` |

The lead of the policy half's message, which is the same text on `PolicyApplyIncomplete` (after the route half's, where that leads), on `GovernanceSkipped`, and on `Ready` and `Degraded` only where no route reason outranks it:

| Clause `policyReport` returned | Route ACCEPTED | Route REFUSED | Route UNKNOWN, either row |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clauseUnattached` — the synthetic `StatusSummary` ancestor, or `Attached=False` on the assayd Gateway's ancestor | "this Agent's route is accepted and SERVING while the assayd Gateway reports that it does not attach the `<agent>-auth` policy, so the route may be answering with no credential required", and "The hole is announced, not closed" | hedged, in full: "the assayd Gateway reports that it does not attach this Agent's `<agent>-auth` policy. Whether the route is answering with no credential required depends on the route, and THIS PASS DID NOT READ IT AS ACCEPTED: PolicyApplyIncomplete also carries the route's own reading, under ServingRouteNotAccepted, and if it says the route is refused then nothing is reaching this Agent at all and this half is the smaller of the two problems:", and "The hole is announced, not closed". Until A85 it said "PolicyApplyIncomplete names the route's own reading first", false wherever a higher-ranked or unranked reason leads the pass (§8.1 item 12) | with `routeRefused` standing, as REFUSED. With NO `routeRefused` standing (A85, §8.1 item 11): the same first sentence and "… THIS PASS DID NOT READ IT AS ACCEPTED:", then "the route's reading at its current generation is unknown — this pass found no status entry for the assayd Gateway from controllerName agentgateway.dev/agentgateway, the only one assayd reads, reporting both Accepted and ResolvedRefs at that generation or either of them False at it, and no refusal of the route is standing — so no condition on this Agent names a route reading. If the route is serving, it may be answering with no credential required:", and "The hole is announced, not closed". Until A85 this cell carried REFUSED's text, whose "PolicyApplyIncomplete names the route's own reading first" was false here: the sentence is `PolicyApplyIncomplete`'s whole message, which names no route reading |
| `clauseRejected` — `Accepted=False` | "this Agent's route is accepted and SERVING while the assayd Gateway reports that it REJECTED the `<agent>-auth` policy outright …", and "The hole is announced, not closed" | hedged, in full: "the assayd Gateway reports that it REJECTED this Agent's `<agent>-auth` policy outright, so none of this Agent's authentication or authorization is in force at the gateway. Whether the route is answering with no credential required depends on the route, and THIS PASS DID NOT READ IT AS ACCEPTED: PolicyApplyIncomplete also carries the route's own reading, under ServingRouteNotAccepted, and if it says the route is refused then nothing is reaching this Agent at all and this half is the smaller of the two problems:", and "The hole is announced, not closed". Until A85 it said "PolicyApplyIncomplete names the route's own reading first", false wherever a higher-ranked or unranked reason leads the pass (§8.1 item 12) | as `clauseUnattached`'s cell: REFUSED's text with `routeRefused` standing, and the unknown-reading sentence with none (A85, §8.1 item 11) |
| `clausePartlyValid` — `Accepted=True` with a reason other than `Valid` | "the assayd Gateway ACCEPTED this Agent's `<agent>-auth` policy but not the whole of it …"; no claim about the route and no "hole is announced" | the same text | the same text |
| none — a HELD claim: `policyUnattached` standing and the policy reading unknown, or the `-auth` step errored (third table) | "a claim from an earlier pass is standing, and this pass re-derived nothing …"; nothing is raised fresh, the claim is re-asserted | the same text | the same text |

**When the policy half is HELD rather than raised** — `status.auth.policyUnattached` standing and this pass derived no policy report: the Gateway has not reported at the policy's current generation, §5's precondition excluded the policy, or the `-auth` step errored — `holdIncomplete` and `holdGovernance` re-assert the claim instead of `raiseIncomplete` and `appendGovernance`. The claim store is left as it stood, except that an explicit route reading still sets or clears `routeRefused`. Driven on envtest on 2026-09-23 by throwaway rows, not committed, with the Agent's generation moved from 1 to 2 between the raising pass and the held one. **The `ObservedGeneration` of every cell below was MEASURED in A84's fifth revision**, on all eight combinations of the held pass's reading — ACCEPTED, UNKNOWN with no route claim, REFUSED, UNKNOWN with `routeRefused` standing, ERRORED — and the stored `PolicyApplyIncomplete` reason, `AuthPolicyNotAttached` (the raising pass read the route accepted) or `ServingRouteNotAccepted` (it read the route refused); the round-3 independent critique drove the errored rows as well and got the same. `GovernanceSkipped` kept generation 1 in all eight.

| Route reading | `PolicyApplyIncomplete` | `Ready`, `Degraded` | `GovernanceSkipped` |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACCEPTED, or UNKNOWN with no `routeRefused` standing | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, the HELD lead with `heldNote` (or `unjudgedNote`). **If the stored reason is `AuthPolicyNotAttached`**, the condition is carried whole, `ObservedGeneration` kept (measured 1, on ACCEPTED and on UNKNOWN). **If it is `ServingRouteNotAccepted`** — on ACCEPTED, the pass on which the route comes back from refused — the claim is re-raised through `raiseIncomplete` and takes the pass's generation (measured 2). UNKNOWN with no route claim and a stored `ServingRouteNotAccepted` was not driven: clearing `routeRefused` needs an ACCEPTED pass, which writes `PolicyApplyIncomplete` under `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, and no path to that combination was found. `LastTransitionTime` is kept either way | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, the held message | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, carried whole, `ObservedGeneration` kept — unless this pass asserted `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` on it, when that reason stands and the held claim is appended (A85) |
| REFUSED | reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, raised fresh; the held policy claim is appended after ` \| AuthPolicyNotAttached: `, and the pass's generation is stamped (measured 2, for either stored reason) | reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, the route half's message alone | reason `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, carried whole; the route half's note is dropped |
| UNKNOWN, `routeRefused` standing | reason `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, carried, then the held policy claim composed beside it, which stamps the pass's generation (measured 2) | as REFUSED, with the held route message | as REFUSED |
| the `-auth` step ERRORED (no route read) | as the UNKNOWN row matching the claim store, both notes `erroredNote`, and `policyJudgedNote` never appended: policy claim alone, generation kept (measured 1); both claims, restamped (measured 2) | as that row | as that row |

`GovernanceSkipped` is carried WHOLE on every row only when its stored reason is `AuthPolicyNotAttached` **and this pass has not already asserted it `True` with `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy`**; otherwise the claim is appended by `appendGovernance`, which keeps either of those two reasons. **Until A85 the second condition was missing, and carrying the condition whole overwrote a `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` that `reportForeign` or `reportAboveServed` asserted earlier on the same pass** — the defect stated above, discharged as §8.1 item 9.

**The last row of the first table does not keep the stored `ObservedGeneration`, and this is the composed state `PolicyApplyIncomplete`'s hold rule below names.** `holdIncomplete` runs first, finds no `PolicyApplyIncomplete` asserted yet on the pass and a stored one whose reason is `ServingRouteNotAccepted`, and re-asserts that condition whole through `conds.carry`, keeping its `ObservedGeneration` and, through `merge`, its `LastTransitionTime`. The policy half's `raiseIncomplete` then composes beside it under `incompleteOrder`: the reason stays `ServingRouteNotAccepted` and the policy half's message is appended, but its `conds.set` stamps this pass's generation. Measured on envtest on 2026-09-23: a stored condition at generation 1, the Agent edited to generation 2, then one pass with the route unknown and the policy broken — the condition read generation 2 with its transition time unchanged; the same pass with the policy holding left it at generation 1.

**Anything that is not an explicit failure at the current generation is UNKNOWN, and an unknown reading HOLDS whatever the last pass reported — it never clears it.** No entry for the assayd Gateway, no condition of that type, an empty ancestor list, or a condition whose `observedGeneration` is behind the object's, all leave the Agent as the last pass left it, and a standing `ServingRouteNotAccepted` or `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is **re-asserted from stored status**, keeping its `LastTransitionTime` and its `ObservedGeneration` — the `ObservedGeneration` only where the held claim is the stored condition's own reason and nothing else writes `PolicyApplyIncomplete` on the pass: a held `PolicyApplyIncomplete` takes the pass's generation when a route reason is raised or held beside it, and when its stored reason was the route's and the route has since come back (the `PolicyApplyIncomplete` bullet below; the third table, measured) — and marked as carried, exactly as `storedHold` and `seedStoredAbove` carry A75's hold. **What is re-asserted is the stored condition's TIMES, not its message: the message is rebuilt from the report's own text.** Appending, which is what "re-asserted from stored status" reads like and which A81 implemented first, is unbounded, and the bound it runs into is fatal: each note carries text that moves — `%v` of the error for the errored note, whose `errStaleAgent` names resourceVersions the pass's own write then bumps — and the caller's non-transient arm appends the write error AFTER the note, so a suffix comparison de-duplicates neither. Measured in envtest: **240 bytes a pass on the transient arm, 475 on the non-transient one, and at pass 133 the API server refuses EVERY status write for that Agent** (`Too long: may not be more than 32768 bytes`), so `observedGeneration`, phase, `Ready`, `Degraded` and the card conditions all stop moving, during exactly the incident this judgement exists to report. The independent review reproduced it on its own fixture at **+244 and +479 bytes a pass, saturating at errored pass 129** (`reviews/03-a81-review.md`); the few bytes of difference are the Agent's own name and namespace, which the message carries. **It heals on the first pass that neither errors nor holds**, which rebuilds the message — so what it costs is every status write for as long as the errors or the unknown readings last, which in the measured incident is until an administrator fixes the Gateway. A81 first wrote "and it does not heal", which was wrong. **The fix is REBUILDING**, and each note keeps a stable marker so the tests can read it and so the half of the errored note that moves is separable from the half that does not. A81 also cut the fallback at any marker it carried; that was dead code — every caller passes a freshly built message that has never been through a note — and is deleted, with this sentence corrected to stop crediting it (A81; **case 19 (m)** pins the rebuild at three consecutive errored passes on each arm). Only an explicit tuple that is **not** broken, at the object's current generation, clears it. **This has to be written down, because the obvious reading is wrong and A80's own remedy is what makes it wrong**: joining `carriedReason` (below) also makes the `-auth` step *withdraw* both reasons on the way into every pass (`reconcileGateway`), and `PolicyApplyIncomplete` is owned and not sticky, so a pass that read unknown and simply said nothing would retract a report that is still true. A promotion is enough to trigger it: the route write moves the route's generation, the Gateway's report is momentarily behind, and a served Agent on a route the Gateway is still refusing would flip back to `Ready=True`, phase `Ready`, with the clock restarted — the original defect, re-entered through the fix. **What is held is the reason's CLAIM, not the condition object, and that distinction is load-bearing because A80's own ordering makes the claim a message fragment in the ordinary case.** Both new reasons sit at the end of `incompleteOrder`, below `GatewayAuthPolicy`, and `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is appended to a standing `ForeignTrafficPolicy`'s or `GatewayAuthPolicy`'s message on `GovernanceSkipped` by the rule below — so whenever another cause outranks one of them, and whenever the route half outranks the policy half, the stored condition's **reason** belongs to that other cause and a reason match, which is all `storedHold`, `seedStoredAbove` and `carriedReason` do, finds nothing to restore. *(This sentence read "in exactly the states where the appended ranks are exercised at all" until A81; the two halves stand beside each other with neither of the other causes present, which is what the review measured.)* So the rule is stated on the claim, **per condition, because the two conditions restore by different machinery**:

- **`PolicyApplyIncomplete`.** A report that is the stored condition's reason is re-asserted from stored status, keeping its `LastTransitionTime` and `ObservedGeneration`, as `seedStoredAbove` carries A75's — **with one exception, which A81 states rather than leaves untrue**: when the pass has already asserted the condition, both halves held or another cause standing, the claim composes through `raiseIncomplete`, whose write stamps THIS pass's generation. The same happens the other way round: when the route half's claim is carried whole and the policy half then raises or holds beside it, that write stamps this pass's generation on the composed condition. **And a SECOND exception, with nothing composed**: a held policy claim whose stored condition's reason is `ServingRouteNotAccepted` — the pass on which the route comes back accepted — is re-raised through `raiseIncomplete` and takes this pass's generation. Every cell measured (A84, the third table above). `LastTransitionTime` survives either way, through `merge`, and it is what design 10's duration rule reads. A report the stored condition carries only inside another reason's message is re-appended through `raiseIncomplete` to whatever reason this pass derives, and if no other reason stands it becomes the reason and keeps the stored `LastTransitionTime`.
- **`GovernanceSkipped`.** What re-asserting the stored condition BUYS on this condition is narrower than it reads, and A81 states it because the rest of it is not reachable: with neither `ForeignTrafficPolicy` nor `GatewayAuthPolicy` standing, the append rule below makes `AuthPolicyNotAttached` the reason anyway, and the message is rebuilt either way, so **what the restoration alone preserves is `ObservedGeneration`** — the generation that observed the report, where a fresh write would stamp the generation of a pass that observed nothing. The fail-open failure is the OTHER rule, one that appends while keeping the reason the pass derived; case 19 (k)'s fourth half kills both, and asserts the generation because without that assertion deleting the restoration leaves the suite green (A81). `raiseIncomplete` cannot be the vehicle here: it hardcodes `PolicyApplyIncomplete` at every one of its writes. And the condition is owned **and sticky**, so a stored value always exists — `assessGovernance` rewrites the *pass's* assertion, never the stored one, and `seedStoredAbove` already restores this condition **whole**, over `assessGovernance`'s fresh value, for `ForeignTrafficPolicy` and for W1's `GatewayAuthPolicy`. So: a stored `GovernanceSkipped` whose **reason** is `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is re-asserted whole on that same precedent, keeping its `LastTransitionTime` and `ObservedGeneration` and carrying the hold marker — **unless this pass has already asserted `GovernanceSkipped=True` with `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy`**, in which case the held claim is appended to that reason's message by the composition rule below, exactly as a raised claim is; only a claim the stored condition carries as a **fragment under another reason** is re-appended to whatever this pass derived, by the same rule. *(The `unless` clause is A85's, §8.1 item 9: without it the whole-restore overwrote the reason §5 says stands, and after a foreign takeover of the `-auth` name the tier condition never named the foreign policy.)* **Getting this backwards is fail-open and is why it is spelled out**: in the ordinary policy half — no foreign policy, no Gateway-level policy — the stored reason *is* `AuthPolicyNotAttached`, and `assessGovernance` has already derived `False`/`AuthVerifiedOnOneReplica` for a served API-key Agent, so a rule that only ever appends leaves the Agent reading `GovernanceSkipped=False`, "auth verified on one replica", while its `-auth` is attached to nothing. That is the claim §3.3.3 and §5 require to read `True`, retracted on every unknown or errored pass.
- **How a fragment is recognised, and what it costs.** Not by parsing the message. The only store today would be a concatenated human-readable string whose `" | "` separator `raiseIncomplete` and `reportAboveServed` both reuse, so a fragment's extent is ambiguous and nothing in the shipped operator reads a condition message for state. **The claim is recorded where the rest of this judgement's state already lives**: two booleans on `status.auth`, one per reason, set when the judgement raises the claim and cleared when an explicit not-broken tuple clears it, so a held pass reads them rather than the message. The fields are `status.auth.routeRefused` and `status.auth.policyUnattached`, named in §3.3.1's block, and **both ship in `config/crd/` and `charts/assayd/crds/` since A81**. **That carries the `crds/` hazard the (A2) cell states, and `authKept` does NOT cover it today** — the chart ships the CRD under `crds/`, which `helm upgrade` never updates, so every CRD in the field predates these two fields and prunes them without an error; and `authKept` compares `mode` and four transaction fields and nothing else, so `persistStatus` returns nil, the operator goes on writing to the gateway, and the hold degrades silently to the fail-open behaviour this rule exists to prevent. **What would make it true is one line: `authKept` gains the two fields**, so a pruning CRD is refused as `AuthRecordNotKept` exactly as a lost `mode` is. **A81 wrote that line, and measuring it corrected this sentence: it reaches LESS than the sentence claims.** `authKept` is consulted only from `persistStatus`, and a served Agent with an empty slot calls it on no pass at all — `reconcileServed` writes the route, the policy and conditions and never `status.auth` — so for the class the store matters most for, a pruning CRD still drops the flags silently and the hold still degrades to the fail-open behaviour. It IS reached on every pass of a refused `Adopt`, whose `refuseAdopt` writes `status.auth` each time, and on a route re-create, a missing-policy `Lock`, an abandonment and every transaction stage. **And `refuseAdopt` had to gain a line A80 does not name**: it carries the stored flags onto the record it rebuilds. Without that its write clears the flag, the judgement sets it again in the same pass, each write re-enqueues the Agent, and a refused `Adopt` on a route the Gateway refuses hot-loops for as long as it exists — and `authKept` would compare two values that are always both false, so the one line above would reach nothing for this class either. The judgement still reads the flags from STORED status, which is what makes it correct whatever `refuseAdopt` does (A81). *(Rule 7; `reviews/03-a80-critique5.md` MINOR 4.)* It is the honest price of a rule that must be computable. A marker written into the message instead was considered and rejected for the reason above. **Every other write that assigns `status.auth` WHOLESALE carries the store across, for `refuseAdopt`'s reason — none of them read the route or the policy, so none has an explicit not-broken tuple to clear a claim with**: a J2 abandonment, and `enterLock` entering K2's `Lock` over a refused `Adopt`. `recordServed` is the one exception and it is the clearing rule rather than a hole in it: a transaction reaching `Served` got §3.3.2's FULL tuple at the object's current generation, which is exactly the explicit not-broken reading §3.1 says clears a standing report. A never-served `Create`'s abandonment writes no `status.auth` at all. *(Four writers dropped the store silently until A81, which makes the clearing sentence above true as written.)* *(`reviews/03-a80-critique4.md` MAJOR 3.)* Without this the everyday cost is the message dropping the Gateway's refusal on one pass and naming it again on the next, which is the flap the hold exists to stop; and the fail-open cost is real though it needs a coincidence — the outranking cause clearing on the same pass the reading goes unknown, after which nothing re-raises and `Ready` returns to `True` on a refused route. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique3.md` MAJOR 2.)*

**A pass whose `-auth` step ERRORED holds the same way, and this is the sentence that keeps the fix from re-entering the defect a second time.** The judgement below runs only on a pass where that step returned no error — but that scope governs **raising**, never clearing. A pass that errored re-derived nothing, so a standing `ServingRouteNotAccepted` or `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is re-asserted from stored status exactly as an unknown reading holds it, on the same claim rule — **and the restoration repopulates `gatewayOutcome.withhold` and `gatewayOutcome.served` with it**, because the condition alone does not withhold `Ready`: `withholdReady` is the only writer of `Ready=False` and it reads those two fields. The caller's error tail must then admit that withhold, which is the one change A80 makes outside the judgement and is stated below rather than left implied. Without both halves this paragraph ships `PolicyApplyIncomplete=ServingRouteNotAccepted` beside `Ready=True`, phase `Ready`, and no `Degraded` — the defect on a third consecutive path, now with a self-contradicting status beside it. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique4.md` MAJOR 1.)* **Nothing in the shipped machinery does this for these two reasons**, and it has to be said rather than assumed: `carriedReason` is also the WITHDRAW predicate at the top of `reconcileGateway`, and everything that puts the condition back on an error is reason-specific and names neither — the recapture pair catches only `AuthPolicyMissing` and `AuthLockUnverified`, and `storedHold` catches only `GatewayAuthPolicy` beside a `Create` or `Lock` at `ProbingAfter`, which a served Agent with an empty slot fails twice over. On the **transient** arm — a `Conflict`, an `AlreadyExists`, a lost route race, a stale cached Agent — the caller takes none of its three arms for such an Agent, the condition is dropped as owned-and-not-sticky, and `Ready` and the phase keep the `True` the rollout switch set above: **a served Agent on a route the Gateway is still refusing would read `Ready=True` with the clock restarted**, which is this paragraph's own sentence one path over. On the **non-transient** arm the write error's reason must **compose** through `raiseIncomplete` rather than replace the standing one, so the Gateway's refusal is not erased by a failed write. A75 built both halves of this for its own hold — `storedHold`'s restoration, and `reportAboveServed` running on `err == nil || transientRouteWrite(err)` under the comment that W1 must not clear for a pass — and A80 inherits neither by construction. The window is one reconcile and self-heals, and in the measured incident nothing writes and nothing errors, so it is narrow; it is written down because the one property this amendment exists to establish is that the operator does not report healthy while the Gateway refuses the route. Case 19 (l) pins the restoration, and **(m) pins that the restored message does not grow** (A81). *(`reviews/03-a80-critique3.md` MAJOR 1.)*

**Which marker a held report carries.** Not `carriedNote`, whose words are "this pass returned before the `-auth` step and did not read the Gateway again" — false of a held report, which reached the step and did read the object, and found no report at its current generation. A hold carries a note of its own: *carried from the last pass that got a report at this object's generation; the Gateway has not reported since*. **There are three markers, not two.** `carriedNote` for a pass that returned before the `-auth` step; the hold note above for a pass that reached the step and read no report at the object's current generation; and a third for a pass whose step errored, which read nothing and says so, naming the error — *carried across a pass whose `-auth` step could not complete; the objects were not re-read*. Putting `carriedNote`'s cause on a held condition would be rule 8 in the small. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique3.md` MINOR 6.)*

**The cost of holding, stated rather than discovered**: a report whose cause has actually gone stays raised until the Gateway reports a good tuple at the current generation, so an Agent that was fixed by a route write reads `Degraded` for as long as the Gateway takes to re-report, and for ever if it never does. That is the fail-safe direction, and it buys one thing the miss below would otherwise take: **a report already raised survives a Gateway that goes silent**. *(`reviews/03-a80-recritique.md` MAJOR 1; the human's decision of 2026-09-18 was hold rather than retract. Case 19 (k) pins it.)* The reason is measured rather than argued: every route write bumps the route's generation, a promotion moves `backendRefs` on the serving route, and the Gateway's report necessarily lags — so treating "the tuple does not hold" as a failure would flip a served Agent to `Degraded` on every rollout and page for it. §3.1's clearing rule is narrowed to match, for the **policy** tuple alone, under this same gate. **What the narrowing gives up is named, and it is larger than it first reads**: a Gateway that is present and readable but whose controller has stopped writing route and policy status is detected by **nothing here, for any mode**. A75's read reports a Gateway the operator **cannot read** — `gatewayAuthPolicies` sets `unreadable` only on a `Get` error or a failed policy list — and a Gateway that reads cleanly while reporting nothing passes it silently. That is the failure of a crashed or wedged gateway controller. **Nothing that reads only these objects can close it**, and that is the honest statement rather than a gap left for choice A to fill: there is no heartbeat on a Gateway API route or on an `AgentgatewayPolicy`. `observedGeneration` is the only freshness signal either carries, and it is generation-relative, so a controller that died after writing a correct report at the current generation is indistinguishable from one that is working and has nothing new to say. Reading the Gateway's own `status.listeners` does not close it either — the same controller writes that too — though it does see the **measured** defect, a `parentRef` naming a listener the Gateway no longer lists, without waiting for a route-status write. Closing it needs a liveness signal about the gateway rather than a status read, which is a read A80 does not make. Choice A in §11 put the whole set to the human, with what each does and does not reach, and **the human decided (A1) on 2026-09-21**: only an explicit `False` at the object's current generation is a failure, and an unknown reading holds. **(A4-spec) — reading the Gateway's `spec.listeners`, the one option on that table that still sees the measured defect with the gateway controller dead — was offered and NOT taken**, so **this judgement** reads a Gateway's listeners in neither form and this gap stands exactly as stated above. "Nothing here reads them" was the sentence until A81, and it is false of the operator: `capturingListeners` reads `spec.listeners` on every served pass with a mode, for A75's W1, to decide which listener a Gateway-level policy can take traffic on. That read answers a different question and this judgement does not use it, but the design must not say the operator makes a read it makes (rule 7, A81). It stays a recorded alternative, with its four owed pieces, in §11. *(First stated as "nothing covers it for `auth: none`", which understated it by about half; `reviews/03-a80-critique.md` MAJOR 5. The claim that an option closes it was then wrong in the other direction; `reviews/03-a80-recritique.md` MAJOR 3.)*

**Where the judgement runs and exactly what it writes. Four critiques have now found this paragraph stating the property and omitting a piece of the machinery that produces it, so it is written as a complete instruction: an implementer who does what is listed here, and nothing else, gets the behaviour §5's two rows and case 19's rows assert.**

- **Placement, and the gate evaluated TWICE.** After the `-auth` step, beside `reportForeign` and `reportAboveServed` in `reconcileGateway`, and never inside the step. **The gate above is the slot as the pass FOUND it and as it LEAVES it, and both halves are needed** (A81): a pass that reaches `Served` starts with a transaction and ends without one, and a pass of a served Agent that enters a route re-create or a missing-policy `Lock` does the reverse — both are a transaction's pass, which is what "neither is raised while a transaction that runs stages is in the slot" means. The pre-step half is read beside the claim store, before `gatewayStep`. `runLock` carries out the route it already holds for the same reason: the GATE, not an accident of which path happens to set the field, is what keeps the judgement off a transaction. Case 19 (g) pins the post-step half and (p) the pre-step one. Inside or before it, the transaction and served paths write `PolicyApplyIncomplete` with `conds.set` directly and would overwrite reason *and* message; after it, the judgement merges through `raiseIncomplete` and the ordering below is true. It does **not** share `reportAboveServed`'s gate, which returns on an empty `status.auth.mode` **and** on a transaction being in the slot — a refused `Adopt` trips both — and so would exclude the Agent class the gate above deliberately admits.
- **Which objects.** The route the pass already holds, carried out on `gatewayOutcome` rather than read again, and the policy `reassertServedPolicy` read **after** both of its guards passed, which it is **owed a return for**: it returns `error` alone today, so handing the judged object out is part of what this amendment owes, not something it describes as present. The two route paths differ and the difference is stated rather than averaged: on the API-key path it is `currentServingRoute`'s read from the top of the pass, whose generation the pass has not yet moved, so a promoting pass judges the last answer the Gateway gave; on the `auth: none` and refused-`Adopt` paths the only object is `ensureServingRoute`'s return, which after an update is the post-write object, so a promoting pass reads unknown there and holds. Both are benign because unknown holds. **A refused `Adopt` with no `status.activeRevision` holds no route object at all** — both `ensureServingRoute` calls are guarded on it — so the judgement is skipped on that pass rather than reading one; that Agent is off the air for a different reason, which `Ready` already carries.
- **What it writes, all five, because omitting any one of them produces a status that contradicts this design.**
  1. **`PolicyApplyIncomplete`**, through `raiseIncomplete`, which composes in `incompleteOrder`.
  2. **`GovernanceSkipped`**, for the policy half only, through a composition of its own — `raiseIncomplete` hardcodes `PolicyApplyIncomplete` at every one of its writes and cannot write this condition — following A75's shape: a standing `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` keeps the reason and `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is appended to its message; with neither standing, `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is the reason. The route half writes a note on this condition and never its reason or status.
  3. **`gatewayOutcome.withhold`**, through `withholdInOrder`. This is the only way `Ready` is ever taken back: `withholdReady` is the sole writer of `Ready=False` on this path, and the rollout switch two hundred lines above sets `Ready=True` on every pass. A judgement that raises conditions and populates no withhold ships `PolicyApplyIncomplete=ServingRouteNotAccepted` beside `Ready=True`.
  4. **`gatewayOutcome.served`**, set true for every class the gate above admits — a served `apikey` Agent, a served `auth: none` Agent, and a refused `Adopt`. `withholdReady` is **two** decisions, not one: it sets `Ready=False`, and then `served` decides `Degraded` plus phase `Degraded` over a bare phase `Pending`. `reconcileServed` sets this flag nowhere today, and in the state case 19 (a) builds neither reporter beside the judgement reaches its own setter, so an implementer who omits it gets phase `Pending` **and `Degraded` actively cleared**, because `Degraded` is owned and not sticky. That is the defect `agent_controller.go` records beside the `WorkloadUnavailable` branch — "a path that sets the phase without the condition actively CLEARS it … the identical defect is recorded two hundred lines above; it was reintroduced here and caught by the independent review of A6.10" — and this amendment, whose whole argument rests on a condition staying up, would be the third time. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique4.md` MAJOR 2.)*
  5. **The claim store**, `status.auth.routeRefused` and `status.auth.policyUnattached` — set when this judgement raises the matching reason, cleared when an explicit not-broken tuple at the object's current generation clears it. It is a write of this judgement like the other four, and case 19 (k)'s third half cannot pass without it: it is what makes the fragment rule above computable on the next pass, when the stored condition's reason belongs to another cause. **Both flags are read from STORED status before the `-auth` step**, as `storedHold` is captured before `gatewayStep`, because `refuseAdopt` assigns `status.auth` wholesale on every pass of a refused `Adopt` — one of the three classes this judgement admits, and the one it calls least covered — so a judgement that read them where it uses them would read them wiped, and the store would be inert for that class.
- **On an errored pass, four of the five, from stored status.** The restoration §3.3.3 requires above is not only the condition: it repopulates `gatewayOutcome.withhold` and `served` too, or the pass writes the condition beside `Ready=True`. **The claim store is the one it does not write, and A81 states that rather than leaving a line nothing can fail (rule 5)**: the pass's `status` began as a deep copy of stored status and already carries the flags; every path that assigns `status.auth` wholesale carries them across; and the one that drops them deliberately, `recordServed`, cannot be reached on a pass this judgement runs on, because such a pass began with a transaction in the slot and the gate excludes it.
- **One change outside the judgement, named because A80 makes it.** The caller's error tail reaches `withholdReady` through three arms, and for a served Agent with an empty slot or a refused `Adopt` **none of them fires**: the first needs a `Create` or `Lock` in the slot, the second never calls it, and the third is gated on the withhold's reason being `GatewayAuthPolicy`. **A80 widens that third arm to admit a withhold the `-auth` step left under either of its new reasons.** It is A75's mechanism covering two more causes and reverses nothing A75 decided — but it is a change to a caller arm A75 owns, it is not confined to this design's own conditions, and §11's scope sentences carry it rather than claiming nothing moves. Its reach is stated too: routing the non-transient arm's write error through `raiseIncomplete` instead of `conds.set`, which the errored-pass rule above requires, changes which reason survives for **every** standing reason and not only A80's two — a missing-policy `Lock`'s `AuthPolicyMissing` would then outrank the write error and keep the condition, where today the write error replaces it. That is a behaviour change on a path A75 and A78 own; it needs no ADR, because it reverses no recorded trade, and it is named here so that nobody meets it as drift. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique4.md` MAJOR 1 and MINOR 6.)*

**The cost, stated in the vocabulary the rest of this section uses.** No new object, no new watch, no new requeue, and no new read. The route is already read on every served pass, through the manager's **cache** — the `HTTPRoute` watch is registered whenever the gateway is enabled (`SetupWithManager`), so the object and its status are in the informer. The policy is already read **live**, twice, on every served API-key pass (`authPolicyPresent` and `reassertServedPolicy`), because controller-runtime does not cache unstructured objects; `reassertServedPolicy` holds the whole object, `status.ancestors` included, and its digest-match short-circuit means the steady-state pass still makes no write. **The rate is the passes that already happen**: the route watch carries no generation predicate, so the Gateway's own status write wakes the Agent, and the report is raised on the next reconcile; and a served Agent is requeued at `CardDriftInterval`, 5 minutes, as the backstop for a dropped event. So the raise is bounded at one reconcile after the Gateway's write, and 5 minutes plus one reconcile in the worst case — and **when** design 10 lands, its rule being `PolicyApplyIncomplete` open for more than 5 minutes, the page is that plus its window, so about ten minutes from refusal to page at worst. Nothing pages today: design 10 is not built (below), and that figure is in any case a claim about a document whose own README row records it as awaiting approval. *(This was A80's last unconditional page claim; `reviews/03-a80-critique3.md` MINOR 2.)* Clearing costs the same reads on the same passes: `PolicyApplyIncomplete` is owned and not sticky, so it goes when the pass stops asserting it, and `Ready` returns to `True` through the ordinary aggregation.

**Proposed by A86, not approved and not built: a third half, the key source.** The paragraph above stays true of A80's judgement, and it is not true of this half. This half runs when the gateway is enabled, `status.auth.mode` is `apikey`, and the slot is empty as the pass LEAVES it. That includes the pass that reaches `Served`. It reads the key source that its live `<agent>-auth` selects, with one uncached `LIST` of full `ConfigMap`s. The selector is taken from the live policy under §3.2's UID guard alone. It never uses the digest guard, which an upgrade that changes the render fails permanently. On a pass that entered with the slot empty, the policy comes from `reassertServedPolicy`'s owed second return. On the `Served` pass, which fetches no policy, it comes from one live `GET`. A `LIST` that succeeds and finds no entry in `data` or `binaryData` raises `PolicyApplyIncomplete`, reason `ApiKeySourceEmpty`. Whether `Ready` is withheld is §9 D6's decision, and the recommendation there is K1: yes. The half writes nothing to `GovernanceSkipped`, not even a note, so the held table's `GovernanceSkipped` column above, as A85 left it, is unchanged. A failed `LIST`, a failed policy `GET`, a selector that is not `matchLabels` alone, or no policy of this Agent's is UNKNOWN. It holds any standing claim, under this half's own marker and notes, never a Gateway note. The claim store gains `status.auth.keySourceEmpty`. It is read from stored status before the step and written after it. `authKept` does not compare it. The write reads it back and logs a pruning instead, so an old CRD is never refused. The new reason joins the end of `incompleteOrder`, `carriedReason` and `a80Carried`. `carriedNote` is rewritten whole, because a `LIST` has no generation. One watch is added: a metadata-only `ConfigMap` informer, filtered by label and to run namespaces, with `annotations` and `managedFields` stripped. It only enqueues. The held table above says a held `AuthPolicyNotAttached` in `PolicyApplyIncomplete` is carried whole, with its `ObservedGeneration` kept. That now also needs this half not to write on the pass. §11 A86 has the whole rule, what K6 would add, and the rows it owes as §8.1 case 20.

**Both reasons join A75's carry set** (`seedStoredAbove`, `carriedReason`), for A75's own reason. `PolicyApplyIncomplete` is owned and not sticky, and several paths write status and return before the `-auth` step — a run namespace that cannot be used, an unresolvable pin, a collision. A pass that returns there re-read neither object, and clearing a report nothing re-read would reset `LastTransitionTime`. **That matters because the whole remedy rests on duration** — design 10 alerts on `PolicyApplyIncomplete` open for more than 5 minutes, and a condition that resets never stays open. **But design 10 is NOT BUILT, and no alert rule ships anywhere in this repository**: `charts/assayd/templates/` renders no alerts and no dashboards, the word does not appear in `charts/` or `config/`, and `docs/designs/README.md` records design 10 as awaiting approval. So **today nothing pages for either reason**. What a user sees is a condition on the Agent — `Ready=False`, phase `Degraded`, and `PolicyApplyIncomplete` with its reason and message — found by `kubectl get agent`, by a human, or by whatever the operator of the cluster has wired to conditions. The carry set and the hold rule are what make the duration meaningful **when** design 10 lands; until then they are what keep the condition from flapping in front of whoever is reading it. The debt is older than A80 — §5's A75 rows already say "a page after 5 minutes" — and A80 is the amendment that rested its central claim on it, so it is corrected here and every page claim A80 makes is written as conditional. *(Rule 7; `reviews/03-a80-recritique.md` MAJOR 4.)* **The carry is a block of its own in `seedStoredAbove`, gated on this judgement's three classes, not an addition to the W1 block beside it.** W1's block returns unless `status.auth.mode` is `apikey` **and** no transaction is in the slot, which excludes a served `auth: none` Agent and a refused `Adopt` — two of the three classes the route half covers — so adding the new reasons to the nearest sibling would carry nothing for them, and an early-return pass would drop their `ServingRouteNotAccepted` and reset the clock. Each carried message says it is carried, and carries A75's staleness caveat with it. *(`reviews/03-a80-critique5.md` MINOR 5.)* *(Both reasons were outside the carry set; `reviews/03-a80-critique.md` MAJOR 4.)* **Design 10's alert text is now wrong for four of the reasons that fire it** — its parenthetical reads "a route is withheld, so traffic is being refused", which is false for `ForeignTrafficPolicy` and `GatewayAuthPolicy` already and for both of A80's: on the route half the Gateway is refusing the route, and on the policy half the route is serving. The alert still fires, because it keys on the type and a duration. The rewording is owed to design 10 and design 10 is not edited from here.

**Where the two new reasons sit among the others, on BOTH conditions.** `GovernanceSkipped` has no `incompleteOrder` — nothing orders it, and the last writer wins — so `AuthPolicyNotAttached` follows §3.2's reason order by hand, the way A75 already does it in code: **a standing `ForeignTrafficPolicy` or `GatewayAuthPolicy` keeps the reason, and `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is appended to its message; with neither standing, `AuthPolicyNotAttached` is the reason.** Without that clause the judgement runs last, under the placement above, and silently retires W1's `GatewayAuthPolicy` or §3.2's `ForeignTrafficPolicy` from the condition that records the tier — both states are reachable beside a policy the Gateway does not attach, and both already have built coverage. *(`reviews/03-a80-recritique.md` MAJOR 2. Only `PolicyApplyIncomplete`'s order was stated, and "appending leaves what those two report unchanged" was true there and false here.)* **When both halves fire on one pass**, the policy half's `GovernanceSkipped=AuthPolicyNotAttached` is written after the route half's note, so the note is replaced rather than kept; that is deliberate and cosmetic, because `PolicyApplyIncomplete` names both causes in `incompleteOrder` and is where a reader is sent. On `PolicyApplyIncomplete`, `incompleteOrder` gains them **at the end**, after `GatewayAuthPolicy`: `AuthPolicyMissing`, `ForeignTrafficPolicy`, `GatewayAuthPolicy`, **`ServingRouteNotAccepted`, `AuthPolicyNotAttached`**. Neither can stand beside a transaction's reason, because neither is raised while a transaction that runs stages is in the slot, and `AuthPolicyNotAttached` cannot stand beside `AuthPolicyMissing`, which needs the object to be absent. **The two stand beside EACH OTHER, which A80 assumed they did not, and that assumption is what its order rested on** (A81). A80 wrote that the only states exercising these ranks are beside `ForeignTrafficPolicy` and W1's `GatewayAuthPolicy`, and put the route half last because leading with it "buys nothing, because the condition's message names every reason that stands either way". **Both sentences are false, and the second is false in a way that matters.** Measured on k3d: renaming the Gateway's listener detaches the route AND leaves `<agent>-auth` attached to nothing, so agentgateway reports `Accepted=False` and writes the synthetic `StatusSummary` ancestor in the same breath, and under A80's order all four conditions then opened with the policy half's "the route may be answering with no credential required" — **announcing a security incident the same pass had refuted**, over the real one, which is that nothing reaches the agent at all. **The route reason now LEADS**: an Agent nothing can reach is the cause to name first, `withholdReady` follows the same order so `Ready` and `Degraded` name it too, and the policy half's message no longer asserts a route reading this pass did not take (§5, case 19 (q)). Appending still leaves `ForeignTrafficPolicy` and `GatewayAuthPolicy` unchanged. *(A80's call, reversed by A81 on a measurement A80 did not have.)*

**Deleting an `Adopt`ed Agent's route is not an exit from `Adopt`.** Its `status.auth` records no `mode`, so the prepared re-create above does not apply. The shipped emitter re-creates the route as before, with `backendRefs` and unauthenticated, and the refusal holds on the next reconcile. Re-creating it through `Create` would lock a route whose callers may hold no key, and nobody asked for it. The human's decision to keep `Adopt` refused (above) rules that out, and a route delete must not do it by the back door. So `Adopt`'s actions stay: recreate the Agent, or K2's edit to `apikey`. *(Settled by A58, `reviews/03-a57-critique.md` MINOR 7. It is an author's call, and it follows the human's decision on `Adopt`.)*

**`Adopt` stays refused** (ADR-0034). The probe machinery its option (d) needed now exists in `Narrow` and, in the slice, in `Lock`, which is the same mechanism (above). `Adopt` is not rebuilt on it. The human decided on 2026-09-12 that it stays refused, and what keeps it refused is consent, not the mechanism (above, and ADR-0034 Amendment 3).

**`Adopt`: a first policy on a route that is already serving is refused.** An operator with `gateway.enabled: true` and no compiler publishes an unauthenticated `<agent>-serving` route for each Agent (§3.1's `PolicyCompilerAbsent` row). An operator upgraded to carry the compiler finds those routes serving with no `-auth`. None of the other kinds fits. It is not `Create`, because the route exists. It is not `Loosen`. A first application classifies as `Tighten` (below), and `Tighten` mints a revision — but no Agent spec moved, so none mints. The obvious patch is to write the policy onto the live route and trust its conditions, and that is exactly the in-place tightening this subsection forbids: a NACK leaves the open configuration serving while every condition reports converged (§3.3.2, spike §2.8), so the slice would record authentication that is not enforced. *(That was ADR-0034's reason, and `Lock`'s probe has since answered it. The refusal now rests on consent, above.)*

So it is refused. The trigger is a published serving route for an Agent that has **no operator-emitted `-auth`**, judged by §3.2's name-and-label rule so that a foreign policy on the route does not count, and whose `status.auth` is absent, or holds nothing but a refused `Adopt`'s own record: no `mode`, and no `Create` or `Lock` transaction. So no compiler has recorded a served `-auth` state for it, and none is part-way through recording one. A missing policy beside a `Create` or `Lock` transaction re-enters that transaction at its write. *(Corrected by A58, `reviews/03-a57-critique.md` MINOR 1. The trigger was `mode` absent. `Create` attaches `backendRefs` at `Publishing` and records `mode` only at `Served`. A crash, or a concurrent delete of `<agent>-auth`, between the two made the next reconcile an `Adopt`, which overwrote the `Create` record and left the route open for good, with no page.)* *(Corrected by A57. The trigger was "`status.apply` absent". The slice records `-auth` in `status.auth`, so `status.apply` is always absent there, and a served Agent whose `<agent>-auth` was deleted read as `Adopt` (`reviews/03-a56-critique.md` M1). That case is now `Lock`, above.)* An earlier version of this sentence, and of the table above, said "no governing policy". A foreign policy made that false while leaving the route exactly as ungoverned (`reviews/03-a53-critique.md` M3). The compiler then:

- writes **no policy** and attaches **nothing** to the route. It does not freeze the route either. The shipped emitter (design 07 A6.10) keeps owning the route's `backendRefs`, so the Agent serves as it did before the upgrade, and **new revisions of an Adopted Agent keep promoting onto an unauthenticated route** until the Agent is recreated. An earlier version of this bullet said `Adopt` "writes nothing to the route" and, in the same sentence, that its `backendRef` follows promotion. A promotion is a route write, so the first half was false;
- records `status.auth.transaction` as `{kind: Adopt, stage: Refused, refusedMode}`, with no `mode`, so the trigger still holds on the next reconcile. The slice writes no `status.apply`;
- sets **`GovernanceSkipped=True`, reason `CompilerUpgradeUnsupported`**. The message names the route and says it is unauthenticated. It says the route has no compiler record, which means it was published before the compiler **or its status was lost**, for example by a backup restore. It names the action: **recreate the Agent**. A recreated Agent has no route, so it enters `Create` and is published only once its `-auth` converges. It also says how K2 ends the refusal: while `refusedMode` is not `apikey`, editing `auth` to `apikey` locks the route in place; while it is `apikey`, the spec already asked for a key before the refusal, so the owner edits `auth` to `none`, waits until `status.auth.transaction.refusedMode` reads `none`, then edits it to `apikey`, or recreates the Agent. An edit made before a reconcile observes `none` is coalesced and does not count. Where another mandatory concern does not compile, for example a stored `spec.budget`, the message says to remove it first, because no `Lock` is entered until it does (§3.3.1) (K2, below);
- re-derives `Adopt` on every reconcile, spec edits included. No spec edit emits a policy or records a `mode`, so the trigger holds again, **except K2's edit to `apikey`, below**. The loop is consistent, and it is stated so that nobody "fixes" it. *(K2's exception added by A66, `reviews/03-a65-check.md` MAJOR 3.)*

**An owner's edit to `apikey` ends the refusal (K2, decided by the human on 2026-09-12, ADR-0034 Amendment 4).** The refused `Adopt` records `refusedMode`. The first refusal sets it to the desired mode, and every later reconcile at which the desired mode is not `apikey` sets it to that mode again. A desired `apikey` never overwrites it. So when the desired mode is `apikey` and `refusedMode` is not, a reconcile has observed the Agent under another mode since the refusal, and the owner has moved it to `apikey`. *(Made to track by A66, `reviews/03-a65-check.md` MAJOR 2, option (a). A65 kept the first value for good, so an owner refused under `apikey` who edited to `none` and back never reached K2, while the message told them the edit would work.)* That is the consent Amendment 3 found missing. The status update that sees the edit replaces the `Adopt` record with a J2 `Lock`, `{kind: Lock, targetMode: apikey, targetDigest}` from the spec. From there it is J2's `Lock` in every respect: `ProbingBefore`, `ApplyingPolicies`, `Converging`, `ProbingAfter`, `Served`, the deadline table's J2 row, and `AuthLockPending` until `Served`. At `Served` it records `mode: apikey`, and it is one-way (§1.1). It is not a re-creation, because no `mode` is recorded (§3.3). So an edit away from `apikey` before `Served` abandons it (below): the policy it wrote is deleted, and the next reconcile is a refused `Adopt` again, with `refusedMode` recorded afresh. An Agent whose spec already said `apikey` when it was first refused records `refusedMode: apikey`. It stays refused until a reconcile observes it under another mode and then under `apikey` again. The operator cannot tell a value an owner set before the upgrade from one a restore brought back, and only an edit observed after the refusal is taken as consent. That boundary is the author's reading of K2, not the human's (ADR-0034 Amendment 4), and so is counting a move from `oauth`. *(Added by A65.)*

**The name is a reason on `GovernanceSkipped`, not a new condition type, and that is deliberate.** The state is precisely "this Agent's gateway path is ungoverned", which is what that type means. Its normal-true, owned classification (§3.1) lets it flip to `False` once the Agent is recreated, or once K2's `Lock` reaches `Served`, rather than lingering. The reason sits beside the operator's own `PolicyCompilerAbsent`, in the same vocabulary. Design 10 keys on the **reason** (§3.1), so it **could** page on `CompilerUpgradeUnsupported` without paging on `GatewayDisabled`. **It does not.** Design 10 §5 says `GovernanceSkipped` "is never an alert" (`10:50`), so an unauthenticated serving route that shows only as this reason is silent in practice. **Owed to design 10**: an alert keyed on `GovernanceSkipped=CompilerUpgradeUnsupported`, a ticket at least since the Agent serves as before, and the same for `ForeignTrafficPolicy`. Design 10 is not edited here. An earlier version of this sentence said design 10 "can page" on it, which design 10's own §5 contradicts. `Ready` is not withheld: the Agent serves exactly what it served before, and a fleet that goes un-`Ready` on upgrade would read as an outage that did not happen. Nothing implements any of this yet.

**The documented future path is option (d), and it is NOT implemented.** `Narrow`'s probe (above) is the same machinery, so (d) no longer needs one of its own. It does not replace the refusal: the human decided on 2026-09-12 that `Adopt` stays refused (ADR-0034 Amendment 3), so (d) is recorded, not adopted. Apply the `-auth` policy onto the serving route in place, converge it, then run an **enforcement probe**, and only then flip `GovernanceSkipped` to `False`. The probe is an anonymous request through the Gateway to the route's hostname, and it must get `401`. That is safe where the in-place tightening forbidden above is not, for two reasons:

- **The prior state was already open.** A NACK that leaves it serving changes nothing a caller can observe. The fail-open that rule exists to prevent is the state *before* this transaction, not a consequence of it.
- **The probe keeps status honest.** Until an anonymous request is refused, the condition keeps saying the route is ungoverned, so the worst outcome is a true statement that the upgrade has not taken yet.

The probe asserts a **transition**, not a value. Before the apply, the same anonymous request gets the agent's own answer, because the route is open and that is the state being adopted. After the apply, it gets `401`. A backend that returned `401` to anonymous callers would fail the "before" half, so the attribution gap this subsection names for a bare `401` does not arise here. `TestTheGatewayRefusesADisallowedPrincipal` already waits on exactly this probe (`waitForEnforcement`) before it trusts anything else. Two things (d) would still owe: a probe that runs with no credential at all, and a statement of what one probe proves when there is more than one gateway replica, which would be `Narrow`'s replica rule (above).

**`Loosen` needs a comparator, and "admitted set" is not one.** Rate limits are stateful quantities, transforms are functions, timeouts are neither, so "every concern's admitted set is a superset" is not implementable and two reasonable implementations classify the same edit differently. The comparator is a **closed registry, one entry per concern**:

| Concern | Ordering | `Loosen` when |
|---|---|---|
| `-auth` | **on the effective admitted-principal policy**, not the mode enum | the new policy admits a **proved superset** of principals — which in practice means `→ none`, byte-identical policy, or an `apikey` policy whose admitted groups are a superset under the same key source. Anything else is `Tighten`, and on the per-Agent serving `-auth` that is §3.3.3's `Narrow`, not a new revision |
| `-ratelimit` | numeric on the derived rate | the new rate is **≥** the applied one |
| `-toolfilter` | set inclusion on tool names | the new set is a **superset** |
| `egressEnumerated` | set inclusion on endpoint identities | the new set is a **superset** |
| `taskTimeout` | numeric | the new timeout is **≥** the applied one |
| `-transform`, `-guard` | **no ordering exists** | never — functions, not sets |

**`oauth == oauth` is not evidence about who is admitted.** The earlier ordering compared `expose.a2a.auth` as an enum, so two OAuth policies admitting disjoint principal sets both normalized to `oauth` and any change between them classified as no-stricter. An identity or IdP input moving the issuer or audience from one tenant to a broader tenant set is precisely that shape: the enum is unchanged, the admitted set is wider, and the update takes the in-place path onto a serving route that no gate ever approved for those principals.

The `-auth` comparator therefore normalizes to the **complete effective policy** — `{mode, issuer, audiences[], claim predicates, principal identity, key/JWKS source identity}`, assembled from `expose` and from design 06's identity inputs. **For the slice's `apikey` mode** the tuple is `{mode: apikey, key source identity, admitted groups}`. Its applied side is read from `status.auth` (§3.3), never from a revision's record, because `-auth` belongs to no revision. The key source is compared as its canonical selector (sorted `matchLabels`, plus the run namespace). The groups are compared as a sorted, de-duplicated set taken *after* §3.4.4's derivation, so an Agent that declares its own namespace and one that declares nothing normalize equal. **The keys themselves are not an operand.** The policy names the `ConfigMap` by selector and agentgateway reads the hashes live, so adding a key to an admitted group widens the admitted principals with no compile and no comparison at all (§3.4.4 names that cost). Three cases are `Loosen`. The two policies are byte-identical after normalization; or the new one removes authentication entirely; or both are `apikey` over the same key source and the new admitted groups are a superset. The last is a proof, not a heuristic: with one key source a key is admitted exactly when its group is in the set, so more groups admit more keys and never fewer. An earlier version of this sentence named only the first two, which classified adding a group as `Tighten`. Every other change, in any field, is `Unknown → Tighten` — and a tightening from a non-spec producer is withheld rather than applied (below), so a narrowing IdP change cannot silently reach a serving route either. Each field is property-tested **independently**: changing exactly one, with the rest held equal, must not classify as `Loosen`.

**Normalization is part of each comparator, because a default is not an absence.** Before comparing, both sides are normalized to their **effective** value: an `expose.a2a.auth` nobody wrote arrives as `oauth`, because the API server persisted the schema default into the stored object and removing the default migrates nothing (§3.4.4), an absent `expose` block is §3.4.4's derived `apikey` policy, an unset `budget` field is *no limit*, an unset `taskTimeout` is the gateway's own default. Comparing raw presence instead would read a field gaining its default as a change, and a field losing an explicit value equal to the default as a loosening.

**Unknown maps to `Tighten`.** A concern absent from the registry, a comparison it cannot make, and a **first application** — where there is no applied set to compare against — all classify as `Tighten` — except a first application to a route that is **already serving**, which no revision can carry and which is the refused `Adopt` above; and on the per-Agent serving `-auth`, where a stricter policy arrives from the current spec or an accepted key-source change, `Tighten` is `Narrow` — so adding a concern without a comparator entry fails safe rather than silently qualifying for the in-place path. Property-tested for reflexivity and transitivity, plus every boundary: a rate unchanged, a set unchanged, a default appearing or disappearing, and `nil` against a value.

**But `Tighten` means "mint a revision", and not every producer can.** §3.1's provenance table lists inputs that are **not Agent spec**: a Connector CR's `toolAllowlist` (11), a resolved KG endpoint (01/13), and `status.llmFallbackActive`, which design 20 sets deliberately. **One** of those three is somebody's spec on another CR — `toolAllowlist`, on the Connector. `status.llmFallbackActive` is a third category again: status on the Agent's *own* CR, controller-written, with no author and no review at all, and for it "cannot mint" is exactly right. Nor is the Connector case softened by review: **nothing gates a Connector edit today** — the repository's two admission policies reserve namespace labels and gateway routes, neither matches `Connector`, there is no webhook, and design 11 states no gate. So what that producer cannot do is mint a revision of **this** Agent; what it also cannot do, contrary to an earlier draft of this sentence, is be caught on the way in. (Tenant consumer budgets were a fourth until they were removed: a tenant's shared limit is not an Agent-scoped input.) Telling those producers to mint a revision points at a mechanism they do not have — so a tool server withdrawing a tool would narrow a mandatory filter with no path at all.

**The table is TOTAL over provenance × comparator result.** The earlier one had a row for non-spec *tightening* and none for non-spec *widening*, and the missing cell inherited the live path — which is the dangerous direction. `tools[].toolAllowlist` is **not** Agent spec, so a Connector author adding `wire_funds` to `spec.tool.toolAllowlist` produces a superset; the comparator calls a superset `Loosen`; and a `Loosen` applies in place. R1's live tool filter would publish a capability R1 was never evaluated with, with **no Agent edit** and no gate — the Agent's own spec and revision are untouched, which is the whole danger. **A later correction fixed the mechanism and left the conclusion standing**: an earlier draft of this paragraph said an MCP *server* that begins advertising a tool produces the superset. It does not — this compiler never reads a server's surface, only the Connector CR (design 11 §4). The superset arrives by a spec edit on a *different* CR, one the Agent's revision gate does not cover. The same shape applies to any externally resolved endpoint set that grows. No cell may inherit a path implicitly, so every cell is written:

| Provenance | `Equal` | `Loosen` (widening) | `Tighten` | `Unknown` |
